TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - TCR-engineered cells demonstrated in vivo survival at 1 month post-treatment in all arms, confirmed by tetramer analysis and TCR staining. This confirms the engineered T cells successfully engaged their NY-ESO-1 target. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The biomarker data confirms downstream biology was modulated - in vivo survival of TCR-engineered cells indicates successful T cell activation and persistence, which is the intended biological mechanism. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Clinical endpoints showed positive results across multiple arms with objective responses (complete and partial responses) achieved in the majority of evaluable patients. Overall response rates were 53% (arm 1), 50% (arm 2), 29% (arm 3), and 60% (arm 4). 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No specific subgroup analysis reported beyond response categories, but responses were seen across different cancer types (melanoma, renal cell cancer, other cancers). 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a single-arm study with multiple treatment variations, making it difficult to isolate individual component contributions. However, the consistent target engagement and clinical responses across arms support the mechanistic hypothesis.

failure_modes.evidence: Small sample size (N=45) across four arms limits statistical power, though objective responses were observed
